A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Gen3R and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, references, and supplementary Sections 6-8. Matching retained content across table renumbering and layout changes supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original generation, reconstruction, camera-control, and ablation results in Tables 1-9 and accompanying qualitative figures.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds held-out-dataset generation and zero-shot reconstruction results in supplementary Tables 8 and 10.

M1.justification: The VGGT geometry adapter, reconstruction and alignment losses, joint appearance-geometry diffusion, conditioning, and decoding procedures remain unchanged. Supplementary architecture details also match; the clarified 2-Stage baseline training does not establish a change to Gen3R.

E1.justification: v2 substantially extends evaluation beyond held-out scenes from training datasets. It adds LLFF, Mip-NeRF 360, and ScanNet++ for one- and two-view appearance generation, plus ScanNet++ for zero-shot geometry reconstruction. These datasets are excluded from Gen3R training; existing training and evaluation coverage is retained.

E2.justification: New Table 8 evaluates SEVA, cited as Stable Virtual Camera, alongside LVSM and Aether. SEVA was not evaluated in v1. Comparator membership in the retained experiments is unchanged; the new reconstruction comparison uses existing baselines Aether and VGGT.

E3.justification: The added evaluations introduce testing on datasets excluded from training: camera-conditioned one- and two-view generation reporting PSNR/LPIPS, and zero-shot ScanNet++ reconstruction reporting accuracy, completeness, and Chamfer distance. Existing experimental settings remain unchanged. The new tests do not specify sample counts or detailed selection procedures.

E4.justification: Supplementary Sections 7.1-7.2 add explicit distribution-shift and zero-shot generalization tests across generation and reconstruction, addressing performance outside the training datasets. This substantially expands the questions investigated beyond the retained joint-generation, alignment-loss, and RGB-head ablations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added results retain the existing practice of reporting single aggregate scores.

E6.justification: New Table 8 reports Gen3R leading all one-view PSNR/LPIPS comparisons, while LVSM leads five of six two-view comparisons. New Table 10 reports ScanNet++ Chamfer distance of 0.1209 for Gen3R versus 0.1279 for VGGT, but worse accuracy, 0.1455 versus 0.1396. These add substantial generalization findings; all numerical entries from v1 Tables 1-9 are retained.

T1.justification: Equations 1-15, latent definitions, reconstruction losses, and KL alignment formulation are unchanged. Neither version supplies additional propositions, proofs, or formal derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: bridging reconstruction and video diffusion through aligned geometry and appearance latents, flexible conditioning, strong scene generation, and improved reconstruction robustness. The added generalization evidence does not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: v2 newly interprets the held-out evaluations as evidence of generalization to unseen scenes. Section 7.2 explicitly acknowledges VGGT's better ScanNet++ accuracy while interpreting Gen3R's better completeness and Chamfer distance as supporting reasonable generalization. Existing mechanism explanations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 4.4 newly specifies that the 2-Stage baseline's video diffusion model was fine-tuned on the authors' training set. Section 4.1 clarifies that explicit 3D ground-truth representations are unnecessary. These are documentation refinements; architecture details, training budgets, hardware, and project-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references including Matrix3D, Dens3R, additional NeRF and Gaussian-splatting research, the new evaluation datasets, and Stable Virtual Camera. These broaden citation coverage and support the added experiments without substantially changing Gen3R's positioning relative to prior reconstruction and generation methods.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording clarifications, slightly edits the conclusion, adds an acknowledgement, and inserts short supplementary discussions of the new evaluations. The narrative, section hierarchy, and most existing prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 restyles the method schematic in Figure 2 and adds supplementary Tables 8 and 10. Existing camera-pose and RGB-reconstruction tables become Tables 9 and 11, with associated text reflow. Qualitative examples and the overall two-column presentation are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens the existing empirical study with evidence on datasets excluded from training and clarifies the 2-Stage baseline's training, improving assessment of generalization and comparison fairness. The added tables also expose limits relative to LVSM and VGGT. The gain is bounded: the method and earlier findings are unchanged, and sample counts and selection procedures for the new evaluations remain unspecified.
